turns.prompt: This is an automated test. Compare tea and coffee on caffeine, taste and price in a Markdown table, then give two tips as a bulleted list.
turns.message:
Tea is the gentler, cheaper sip; coffee hits harder on caffeine but costs more. Here's the breakdown:

| | Caffeine (per 8 oz) | Taste | Price (per cup, homemade) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tea** | ~30–50 mg | Lighter, tannic, floral/green to malty black; varies a lot by type | ~$0.10–0.30 |
| **Coffee** | ~95 mg (drip) | Richer, roasted, bitter-to-sweet; bolder and more consistent | ~$0.20–0.60 |

Café prices flip the gap wider — a coffee out is usually 2–4× a tea.

- **Steep tea at the right heat (green ~80°C, black ~95°C) and don't over-steep** — most "bitter tea" is really just burnt leaves, same as scorched coffee.
- **Cut caffeine after ~2 pm** — coffee's ~95 mg lingers 5–6 hours, so it can quietly wreck your sleep even when you feel fine at night. (Unless you're the lucky type who sleeps through anything.)
